sections.h2: Who records deeds in Sherburne County?
sections.html:
The Sherburne County Recorder's Office keeps the real estate records for every property in the county, including deeds, mortgages and other filings. Staff examine each document to confirm it has the required information before it is recorded.

The office is at 13880 Business Center Drive NW, Suite 100, Elk River, MN 55330-4668, and the phone number is 763-765-4420. Some services need an appointment, but the county says no appointment is needed to record a document. It also issues certified birth and death records, which is separate from property work.

sections.h2: How do I get a deed recorded in Sherburne County?
sections.html:
The county strongly recommends eRecording and points businesses to the Minnesota Land Title Association directory to find a title company that can submit electronically. Most sellers never file directly, because the closing agent handles it. If you file on your own, mail or bring the original to the address above.

Once a document arrives, the recorder follows a fixed sequence:

  1. Review it for completeness against state requirements
  2. Check that the correct fees came with it
  3. Assign a sequential number and stamp the date and time
  4. Index by legal description
  5. Index by grantor, grantee and more than 20 other fields
  6. Verify the indexing
  7. Scan the document and check the image
  8. Prepare a receipt and return it to the presenter

Recording means the document is reproduced and returned to the presenter, while filing means the office keeps the original. The office does not give legal advice or prepare documents, citing Minnesota Statutes 481.02, so see a real estate attorney if you need a deed drafted.

sections.h2: Why would the recorder return my deed?
sections.html:
The county lists the most common reasons real estate documents come back unrecorded. Check each one before you send anything.

  • Delinquent real estate taxes are due
  • The draftsman statement is missing
  • The deed tax or mortgage registration tax is wrong
  • The legal description is inconsistent with the records or questionable
  • The Certificate of Real Estate Value is missing or incomplete
  • The name and address for future tax statements is missing
  • The notary acknowledgment is incomplete
  • The recording fee is wrong
  • Well information is missing from a transferring document

sections.h2: What recording fees apply in Sherburne County?
sections.html:
The county posts its fee schedule on its Abstract and Torrens title pages, and the amounts track the caps in Minnesota Statutes 357.18.

Selected Sherburne County Recorder fees from the county's Abstract and Torrens title pages
ItemFee
Recording a deed or other document (Abstract)$46
Well certificate$54
Certified copy$10 flat
Non-certified copy submitted with the original$2
Multiple satisfactions or assignments, up to 4 citations$46, plus $10 for each citation over four
Plat$56
Returned check$30
Transfer of a Torrens certificate$46

The county says it does not collect a conservation fee. Deed tax, mortgage registration tax and the Certificate of Real Estate Value are handled by the Auditor/Treasurer's Office, so call that office for the right amounts. Copy and mailing fees listed on the county's Copy and Use Fees page took effect January 1, 2026, and include $2.00 for the first page of a mailed copy.

sections.h2: What is the difference between Abstract and Torrens property?
sections.html:
Minnesota keeps two land systems, and the county records both. With Abstract property, the abstract is a condensed history of every deed, mortgage and other document that affects the land, and an attorney or title insurer reviews it when the property sells. Many Sherburne County abstracts list the recorded homestead documents at the beginning.

With Torrens property, a court directs a certificate of title, and the certificate itself is the title. The County Recorder acts as Registrar of Titles, an arm of the District Court, and an Examiner of Titles advises the Registrar. Under Chapter 508 of Minnesota Statutes, some instruments cannot be accepted for filing unless the Examiner certifies them or a court orders it. If you are not sure which system your parcel uses, call 763-765-4420 before the deed is drafted.

sections.h2: What well disclosure does a Sherburne County deed need?
sections.html:
A transfer document that requires a Certificate of Real Estate Value must also carry well information. If there are no wells, the document says so, with wording such as the seller certifying that the seller does not know of any wells on the described property.

If there is a well, attach a completed Well Disclosure Certificate. A seller who can state that the number and status of wells have not changed since the last filed certificate may skip a new one. To check whether a certificate is already on file, call the Minnesota Department of Health at 800-383-9808 or search its well disclosure database.

sections.h2: How big is Sherburne County, and how fast is it growing?
sections.html:
Census estimates put the county at 104,194 people in mid-2025, a 7.2% rise on the April 2020 base. It had 12,861 people in 1960 and 64,417 in 2000. Elk River is the county seat and largest city.

  • 38,457 housing units and 35,555 households averaging 2.78 people
  • 83.2% of homes owner-occupied
  • Median owner-occupied value of $361,400 and median gross rent of $1,127
  • Median household income of $105,466
  • Mean commute of 30.7 minutes
  • 319 building permits issued in 2025

The county covers 451 square miles, of which 433 are land. The Mississippi forms the southern border, the Rum River crosses the upper east, and the Elk River drains the west and south. Soil holds a lot of sand and gravel from glaciers, so it suits farming less well than much of the state.

sections.h2: How was the county formed, and why do old deeds mention Humboldt?
sections.html:
The territorial legislature carved Sherburne County from the south part of Benton County on February 25, 1856, and named it for Moses Sherburne, a territorial judge. The first county seat was the village of Humboldt, which is now Big Lake. A county vote moved the seat to Elk River in 1867, and Humboldt took the name Big Lake that same year. Elk River was platted as two villages, Orono in 1855 and Elk River Village in 1865, which merged in 1881.

County boundaries have not changed since 1856, so every recorded deed since then sits in the same county's records, even where a village name has changed.

sections.h2: What other recorder services matter in a sale?
sections.html:
Owners can sign up for the free Property Watch alert, which tells them when a document with their name is recorded. The county also offers an escrow account for recording fees with a minimum $200 balance, which prevents rejections for short payment.

  • State tax liens are indexed by taxpayer name, with a $30 fee at release; federal liens and releases are $46
  • Completed foreclosure sales, court records and plat searches are linked from the recorder's page
  • Mortgage foreclosure sales run through the Sheriff at the Government Center on Tuesdays and Wednesdays at 10 a.m.
  • A certificate of redemption from the Sheriff costs $250 and needs a request at least 10 days ahead

Property tax statements go out in March, with a March 31 statutory deadline, and taxes unpaid after the payable year become delinquent. Call the Auditor/Treasurer at 763-765-4350 for a payoff figure before closing.

sections.h2: What does Minnesota require when a Sherburne County house is sold?
sections.html:
When a house sells for more than $3,000, the grantor, grantee or their agent must file a certificate of value with the county auditor at the time of recording, under Minnesota Statutes 272.115. The deed tax is .0033 of the net consideration under section 287.21.

The assessor removes the homestead classification for the following year after a sale, unless the buyer applies and qualifies.

faqs.q: Where is the Sherburne County Recorder located?
faqs.a: At 13880 Business Center Drive NW, Suite 100, Elk River, MN 55330-4668. The phone number is 763-765-4420.

faqs.q: What is the fee for filing a deed with the Sherburne County Recorder?
faqs.a: The recording fee for an Abstract document is $46, and a well certificate adds $54 where one is required. The county does not collect a conservation fee.

faqs.q: Do I need an appointment to record a document?
faqs.a: No. The county states that no appointment is needed to record a document, though some other services require one.

faqs.q: Where do I pay deed tax in Sherburne County?
faqs.a: Contact the Auditor/Treasurer's Office, which handles deed tax, mortgage registration tax and the Certificate of Real Estate Value. The number for property tax questions is 763-765-4350.

faqs.q: Can I check who recorded a document against my name?
faqs.a: Yes. The Property Watch service is a free subscription that notifies you by email or phone when a document is recorded under your name.
